researcher_notes: COMPANY CONFIRMED REAL. Legal entity: Magazino GmbH, Landsberger Str. 234, 80687 Munich, Germany (DE). Amtsgericht Muenchen HRB 209758, VAT DE293308625. Managing directors: Frederik Brantner, Dr. Moritz Tenorth, Lukas Zanger. Founded 2014 (Brantner, Zanger, Engelhard). ~120 employees (IEEE Robots Guide profile; the company's own About page uses a JS counter that curl cannot resolve). Source: https://www.magazino.eu/en/imprint/ . || OWNERSHIP: Jungheinrich was an early investor alongside Koerber, Zalando and Fiege Logistik and later took majority control. Magazino's own About page states verbatim 'since Jungheinrich's acquisition in 2023, our scope goes far beyond these two robots' and 'What started as a small robotics start-up is now the core of Jungheinrich's global robotics and autonomy unit'. The site header brands the company 'MAGAZINO > Jungheinrich > Magazino'. So as of now Magazino is a Jungheinrich company, NOT independent in ownership terms. Source: https://www.magazino.eu/en/about/ . || BRAND STATUS: Magazino still operates and sells under its own brand with its own domain (magazino.eu) and its own product line (SOTO, TORU), but commercial routing is Jungheinrich's: every CTA on the SOTO page reads 'Book a consultation now via Jungheinrich' / 'Schedule a call now with our Jungheinrich colleagues', and the official SOTO technical datasheet is hosted on Jungheinrich's media CDN with a Jungheinrich imprint (doc ID 7777.DE.12.2023.r). Jungheinrich also lists SOTO in its own catalogue (jungheinrich.co.uk/automation/mobile-robots/soto-1684506). DB CONSEQUENCE: keep Magazino as a distinct supplier record, but be aware SOTO may be entered a second time under the existing Jungheinrich supplier record - dedupe check recommended. || PRODUCT SCOPE: exactly TWO vehicle products, both currently marketed. (1) SOTO - autonomous KLT/tote logistics robot for production supply, explicitly positioned as a replacement for tugger-train processes. Classified here as Mobile AMR (it has a gripper + onboard shelf, not forks and not a tow hitch). (2) TORU - autonomous box-picking robot for shoe boxes / special KLTs from shelving racks. Also Mobile AMR (picking support). Both appear in the site's top-level solution navigation ('Production Logistics -> SOTO', 'Commissioning -> TORU'). No third vehicle exists: 'Magazino Fleet Manager', 'ARC (Advanced Robot Control)' and 'ACROS' are software, and 'Jungheinrich Mobile Robots' linked from the Magazino homepage is the parent's portfolio, not a Magazino product. The historical 'TORU Cube' is the superseded first-generation name of TORU and is NOT entered as a separate product. || WHAT IS NOT IN SCOPE: Magazino builds no forklift AGV, no pallet-handling AGV and no tugger AGV of its own. Neither SOTO nor TORU handles pallets - SOTO handles VDA 4500 KLTs (max 600x400 mm), TORU handles individual cartons/KLTs of max 390x280x145 mm. If the tender pipeline expects pallet transport, Magazino will legitimately fail on load_type. || SOURCE QUALITY WARNING: the aggregator sites mobile-robots.com and automatedwarehouseonline.com publish a SOTO payload of '360 kg', which directly contradicts the official Jungheinrich/Magazino datasheet (max. Nutzlast gesamt max. 240 kg). Those aggregators' numeric payload figures are therefore treated as unreliable in this research, and their TORU '40 kg' payload claim was deliberately NOT used. || RESEARCH LIMITATION: WebSearch/WebFetch became unavailable partway through (account spend limit); the remainder was done with curl + pdfplumber. The TORU datasheet that Magazino used to publish (insights.magazino.eu/de/toru-datenblatt-de) now returns HTTP 404, so no current official TORU spec sheet exists - TORU's chassis specs below come from third-party sources and are flagged accordingly.

products.notes: PRIMARY SOURCE: official Jungheinrich/Magazino technical datasheet PDF 'Mobile Robot Behaelter-Handling SOTO' (doc 7777.DE.12.2023.r), text extracted with pdfplumber. Verbatim datasheet rows: Eigengewicht 686-735 kg (695 kg Standardkonfiguration); Tragfaehigkeit 200-249 kg (240 kg Standardkonfiguration); Abmessungen (L x B x H) 2.230 x 1.060 x 2.160 mm (Hoehe in Betrieb zzgl. Laserscanner +80 mm); Antriebsmechanik omnidirektionaler Antrieb; Hoechstgeschwindigkeit 1,5 m/s; Min. Breite fuer sichere Geschwindigkeit (0,3 m/s) / fuer Hoechstgeschwindigkeit = 1.650 mm / 2.510 mm; Min. Wendekreis 3.100 mm; Mind. Greifhoehe (frontal / seitlich) 500 mm / 400 mm; Max. Greifhoehe 1.700 mm; unterstuetzte Ladungstraeger-Abmessungen 300x200, 400x300, 600x400 mm bei Hoehen 80-320 mm (Breite muss immer groesser sein als die Hoehe); Max. Anzahl der KLTs pro Roboter 8 (600x400 mm) bis 24 (300x200 / 400x300 mm); Unterstuetzte Normen VDA 4500 (R-KLT, RL-KLT); Max. Gewicht pro KLT / Max. Nutzlast gesamt = max. 20 kg / max. 240 kg (24 Behaelter a 10 kg); Schwerpunkt der Ladung max. 2/3 zu einer Seite; Drehung des KLT im Inneren des Roboters +/-180 und +/-90 Grad; Schutzklasse IP 20; Temperatur 15-25 C, max. kurzzeitig bis 1 h 35 C; Luftfeuchtigkeit <95% nicht kondensierend; Bodenqualitaet Industrieboden nach DIN 18202:2019-07, Hoehe der befahrbaren Bodenunebenheiten 5 mm; Reinraumzertifizierung ISO-7-Zertifikat; Akku 8x Li-Ion 25,6 V je 21 Ah; Arbeitszeit ohne Laden bis zu 8 Stunden; Ladezeit 1,6 Stunden (Verhaeltnis 5:1); Sicherheitsmerkmale: sicherer Betrieb in der Naehe von Personen durch zertifizierte Sicherheitskomponenten, 2D-Laserscanner und 3D-Kameras zur dynamischen Kollisionsvermeidung; Benutzerschnittstelle 2x Touch-Displays, LEDs; Schnittstelle: Integration ueber VDA 5050 moeglich, alternativ Anbindung des Magazino Fleet Manager ueber standardisierte REST-Schnittstelle an das WMS. || SECONDARY (official product page, https://www.magazino.eu/en/production-logistics/): 'Aisle widths as narrow as 1.65m are fully navigable; from 2.5m wide aisles, SOTO can achieve its maximum speed of 1.5m/s'; 'SOTO uses a flexible gripper mechanism to transfer KLTs between heights of 0.4m and 1.7m from the ground'; 'The gripper can pick up and place containers from three directions: left, right, and front'; 'Barcode scanners on the gripper ensure that the correct tote is picked up'; 'thanks to its powerful Li-ion batteries, it can drive for up to 8 hours without recharging (charging ratio: 1 minute charging = 5 minutes driving)'; 'The KLT robot SOTO is VDA5050-compliant and can also be connected to a 3rd party master controller if you are operating a mixed fleet of robots from several vendors'; 'The SOTO Fleet Manager is connected to your WMS system via an interface'. SLAM navigation confirmed on https://www.magazino.eu/en/products/soto/ ('SLAM technology (Simultaneous Localization & Mapping Process)') and on the tech article https://www.magazino.eu/en/tech-articles/robot-soto-setup-mapping-modeling/. || DERIVATIONS / JUDGEMENT CALLS: (1) max_payload=240 = 'Max. Nutzlast gesamt max. 240 kg' (standard backpack config). The datasheet's separate Tragfaehigkeit row gives a config-dependent range 200-249 kg, and the product page text says 'a total payload capacity of 250kg'. 240 is the conservative datasheet-confirmed figure - see FLAG. (2) charge_time=96 min = 1,6 Stunden. (3) min_turning_radius=1550 DERIVED by halving the datasheet's 'Min. Wendekreis 3.100 mm': German 'Wendekreis' is a turning CIRCLE (diameter). A 3100 mm radius is implausible for a 2230x1060 mm omnidirectional robot whose half-diagonal is only ~1235 mm. If the AP0 field is intended as a diameter, use 3100. MEDIUM confidence on this single field. (4) cleanroom_class: datasheet states 'Reinraumzertifizierung ISO-7-Zertifikat'; AP0 only offers 'None' / 'ISO 1-9', so the real class is ISO 7. (5) floor_flatness_req mapped from 'Industrieboden, Ebenheitsabweichung nach DIN 18202:2019-07' + 5 mm drivable unevenness to the closest AP0 bucket 'Standard (FM2)'. DIN 18202 is not literally FM2 - MEDIUM confidence. (6) lift_height=1700 = 'Max. Greifhoehe 1.700 mm', i.e. the maximum gripper transfer height (min 500 mm frontal / 400 mm lateral). This is a gripper height, not a mast lift height. (7) picking_mechanism='Conveyor-integrated': SOTO uses conveyor-belt grippers ('active gripping technology using conveyor belt grippers') to pull and push totes. (8) rotation_capable=true refers to the robot rotating the KLT internally by +/-90 and +/-180 degrees. (9) vda5050_compatible=true is EXPLICITLY PUBLISHED, not assumed. multi_fleet_capable=true from the 3rd-party-master-controller / mixed-fleet statement. (10) safety_coverage='Limited 3D': 2D laser scanners front and rear for the safety field, plus two 3D cameras for obstacle detection and light curtains at the gripper openings - not a certified full-3D safety envelope. MEDIUM. (11) outdoor_capable=false derived from IP20 + 15-25 C window - high confidence as a negative. (12) load_type: VDA 4500 R-KLT/RL-KLT small load carriers map to both 'Tote' and 'Plastic Bin'. (13) industries_served mapped from the site's own sector navigation (Automotive, Injection Moulding, Electronics, Consumer Goods); named reference customers MAN (fleet of 12 SOTOs), Bosch, WAGO, VEGA. || NOT FOUND - LEFT NULL DELIBERATELY: max_gradient, stop_accuracy, autonomous_charging (charging stations exist and the fleet manager dispatches charging, but no source explicitly confirms autonomous docking; one third-party article mentions inductive charging stations, uncorroborated by the datasheet), battery_swap_capable, safety_standard (the datasheet says only 'zertifizierte Sicherheitskomponenten' - ISO 3691-4 is NOT named anywhere), functional_safety_level, max_fleet_size, manual_usage, min_ground_clearance, throughput_picks_per_hour, storage_system_type, task_interleaving. || NOT REPRESENTABLE IN THE CURRENT FIELD VOCABULARY (AP0 gap worth noting): vehicle height 2160 mm / 2240 mm with laser scanner in operation - Mobile AMR has no height field; minimum corridor width 1650 mm (at reduced 0.3 m/s) and 2510 mm (for full 1.5 m/s) - Mobile AMR has no aisle-width field, only Forklift min_aisle_width and Tugger tugger_min_aisle_width exist. Both are commercially decisive numbers for SOTO. || FLAG: payload discrepancy 240 kg (datasheet, standard config) vs 250 kg (product page prose) vs 200-249 kg (datasheet Tragfaehigkeit range). Used 240.

products.notes: COMMERCIAL STATUS: TORU IS STILL OFFERED. It occupies a top-level slot in the site navigation ('Commissioning - The mobile picking robot TORU takes over the intelligent picking of small boxes'), has a full current product page, and is the core vehicle of an active partnership with NEOintralogistics (pay-per-pick complete system with buffer station and goods-to-employee station). The About page confirms 'We're the team behind SOTO and TORU'. Named customers: Zalando, Gabor, Schuurman, ASICS, BMW Group. Caveat: TORU's go-to-market today looks primarily like the NEO system rather than a standalone vehicle sale, and Magazino's own TORU datasheet download page (insights.magazino.eu/de/toru-datenblatt-de) now returns HTTP 404 - so no current official spec sheet exists. || CONFIRMED FROM MAGAZINO'S OWN PAGES (https://www.magazino.eu/en/products/toru/): 'TORU has a precise vacuum gripper arm. This allows it to pick up, lift and place cartons or special totes weighing up to 5.8 kg, with a max. size of 390 x 280 x 145 mm (L x W x H) ... Even entire stacks if necessary'; 'TORU can transport up to 16 objects simultaneously in its backpack rack. With its action range of 8 cm to 250 cm above the ground'; '2D and 3D cameras - TORU locates objects to be picked and free storage locations on the shelf. Using intelligent algorithms, TORU searches for the barcodes and can thus identify the correct object'; 'Due to the autonomous navigation of the robot, no adjustments by the customer in the form of lines or barcodes on the floor are necessary'; 'The lifting column enables fast, precise positioning of the gripper to any gripping height as well as agile rotation between the storage rack and the backpack'; 'Up to 20 hours a day'; 'The connection to a warehouse management system is uncomplicated via WLAN'; fleet software is 'ARC (Advanced Robot Control)', the 'control center of the TORU fleet ... connected to the inventory management system', incl. a 24/6 remote operations team; transfer stations: conveyor belt, flow rack, order-picking trolley (pick-cart), putwall. From https://www.magazino.eu/en/commissioning/: 'TORU picks safely and efficiently up to a height of 220 cm'; NEO KLT items up to 380 x 240 x 140 mm and 5 kg; 'Simple IT integration into existing WMS system possible with only 10-15 developer days'. || THIRD-PARTY CHASSIS SPECS (IEEE Spectrum Robots Guide, https://robotsguide.com/robots/toru): Length 137.5 cm, Width 68.5 cm, Height 193-291 cm (retracted to fully extended), Weight 235 kg, Speed 5.4 km/h (= 1.5 m/s), '60 sensors, including laser scanners at the front and rear, 2D and 3D cameras, and bumper sensors', 'Perception driven navigation based on simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM)', 'Lithium-iron battery pack, 9 hours operation on a single charge'. The independent mobile-robots.com vendor directory gives the same chassis figures (1375 x 685 x 1930 mm, 235 kg, 1.5 m/s), which is why vehicle_length / vehicle_width / max_speed are entered at MEDIUM confidence despite not coming from Magazino directly. Both entries most likely trace back to Magazino's now-offline datasheet. || DERIVATIONS / JUDGEMENT CALLS: (1) lift_height=2500 from Magazino's own 'action range of 8 cm to 250 cm above the ground' - this is the gripper's maximum reach height, not a mast lift. Note the Commissioning page separately says 'picks ... up to a height of 220 cm' (probably the practical KLT picking height inside the NEO system) - minor internal inconsistency; 2500 mm is the figure Magazino publishes on the TORU product page itself. (2) picking_mechanism='Autonomous arm' from Magazino's own wording 'precise vacuum gripper arm'; physically it is a telescoping lifting column carrying a vacuum gripper, not a 6-axis articulated arm. If the AP0 semantics of 'Autonomous arm' implies an articulated manipulator, 'Bin-transfer' would be the better bucket. MEDIUM. (3) battery_type=Li-Ion at LOW confidence: IEEE says 'Lithium-iron battery pack', which strictly would be LiFePO4; Magazino publishes no chemistry. Li-Ion entered as the family. Consider NULL if strict. (4) battery_runtime=8 h at LOW confidence: sources conflict - IEEE says 9 hours on a single charge, aggregator/datasheet-derived sources say 'battery run time max. 8 hours, operating time max. 18 hours per day', and Magazino's own page says 'Up to 20 hours a day' (duty time including charging, not battery runtime). 8 is the conservative choice. (5) safety_coverage='Single plane (2D)' derived from the sensor list: safety-rated laser scanners front/rear plus bumper sensors; the 2D/3D cameras serve object perception/picking, not the safety field. MEDIUM. (6) autonomous_obstacle_bypass=true from 'navigate fully autonomously, using laser scanners to drive safely around people' - MEDIUM, Magazino's own text does not state bypass explicitly. (7) rotation_capable=true from 'agile rotation between the storage rack and the backpack'. (8) load_type / onboard_container_type: TORU's primary load is an individual shoe CARTON, for which the AP0 vocabulary has no exact bucket; 'Tote'/'Plastic Bin' cover the NEO-KLT variant TORU also handles. Flagged as an AP0 vocabulary gap. (9) industries_served from named customers and use cases (fashion/shoe e-commerce: Zalando, Gabor, Schuurman, ASICS; spare parts and small parts for production/assembly: BMW Group). (10) outdoor_capable=false: indoor rack-picking robot with a 2.9 m telescoping tower; no IP rating published anywhere. Negative asserted with high practical confidence. || NOT FOUND - LEFT NULL DELIBERATELY: max_payload (CRITICAL - this is a KO_IF_LT field. mobile-robots.com states '40 kg', but that same source publishes 360 kg for SOTO where the official datasheet says 240 kg, so its payload figures are demonstrably unreliable. Magazino publishes only the per-box limit of 5.8 kg and a 16-box capacity, and explicitly does NOT publish a total backpack payload. Recommend NULL and, if the value matters for a tender, ask Magazino/Jungheinrich directly), omnidirectional_movement, charge_time, autonomous_charging, battery_swap_capable, operating_temp_min/max, operating_humidity_max, ingress_protection_rating, cleanroom_class, floor_flatness_req, max_gradient, stop_accuracy, min_turning_radius, min_ground_clearance, safety_standard, functional_safety_level, vda5050_compatible (NOT claimed for TORU anywhere - only SOTO is explicitly VDA5050-compliant; do NOT copy the SOTO value across), max_fleet_size, multi_fleet_capable, manual_usage, onboard_ui, throughput_picks_per_hour (the '350+ picks per hour' figure on the Commissioning page belongs to the complete NEOintralogistics SYSTEM - buffer station, cobot arm and goods-to-employee station included - not to a single TORU, so it was deliberately not entered), storage_system_type. || NOT REPRESENTABLE IN THE CURRENT FIELD VOCABULARY: vehicle height 1930 mm retracted / 2910 mm extended; vehicle weight 235 kg; per-object weight limit 5.8 kg and per-object max dimensions 390 x 280 x 145 mm (there is no 'max single load weight' or 'max load carrier dimensions' field); minimum aisle width (Magazino markets TORU's 'narrow lane width required by TORU' as a storage-density advantage but publishes no number).
